* WHERE...Kodiak Island Northeast.

* WHEN...Until 11 PM AKST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Heavy snow and rain on snow may create difficult travel
conditions.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A compact storm will move southeast of Kodiak
Island and remain nearly stationary through Friday afternoon to
evening. Slight deviations in the storm position to the east and
west will cause snow levels to fluctuate between sea level and 400
ft in elevation. Kodiak city and the archipeligo to the north are

temperatures, a lower likelihood of rain, and snow accumulations
from 6 to 10 inches.

properties.headline: Winter Storm Watch issued November 13 at 12:09PM AKST until November 16 at 3:00AM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Moderate to heavy snowfall possible.

* WHERE...Anchorage and Eagle River (all elevations), East Turnagain
Arm, Western Kenai Peninsula, Southern Kenai Mtns, Interior Kenai
Peninsula, and Turnagain Pass.

* WHEN...From Saturday afternoon through late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Longwave troughing in the Bering Sea hedges
east as inverted troughing in the Gulf of Alaska tracks west. A
snow band will set up and stall over Anchorage/Kenai Peninsula
tomorrow afternoon through Sunday bringing rounds of moderate to
heavy snowfall. There is moderate uncertainty as to where the snow
band will ultimately end up, resulting in lower confidence for
snowfall amounts. Warmer temperatures filters in Sunday afternoon
from east to west, transitioning snow to rain.

*Low/High end values are as follows:

- Anchorage/Eagle River & western Kenai Peninsula: 2-4" (Low
end)/6-10" (High end). Higher elevations: up to a foot possible.

- Seward: 1-3" (Low end)/3-6" (High end).

- Turnagain Pass to Moose Pass: 7 to 11" possible.

- Portage: 9-11" with snowfall rates of up to 1" an hour.
properties.instruction: Monitor the latest forecasts for updates on this situation.

properties.areaDesc: South Washington Coast
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 13 at 12:40PM PST until November 13 at 4:00PM PST by NWS Portland OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Warning, large waves and dangerous surf
conditions. Breakers up to 30 to 35 feet. For the Coastal Flood
Advisory, tidal overflow flooding expected.

* WHERE...South Washington Coast.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, until noon PST Saturday. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding, up to one foot above ground level,
during high tides is expected in the low lying areas near bays,
sloughs, and the lower reaches of the coastal rivers.
Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties, and other
structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off rocks and
jetties and drown while observing high surf. Severe beach
erosion may destroy coastal properties and buildings. Higher
than normal water run-up is expected on beaches and low-lying
shoreline.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The threat of sneaker waves is extreme
during these scenarios. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock people
off of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid ocean
which may lead to serious injury or drowning. The sneaker wave
threat will peak Friday evening into Friday night. In addition,
the Toke Point tidal gage is forecast to reach 11.2 feet during
high tide Friday afternoon, which is high enough to result in
tidal overflow flooding for a few hours around high tide.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory means that tidal overflow flooding is
expected. Coastal residents in the warned area should be alert
for rising water, and take appropriate action to protect life and
property.

A High Surf Warning means that high surf will affect beaches,
producing rip currents, sneaker waves and beach erosion. Stay
well back from the water's edge and be alert for exceptionally
high waves.

Keep away from large logs on the beach. Water running up on the
beach can lift or roll logs which can injure or kill someone
caught in their path.

A Coastal Flood Advisory means that tidal overflow flooding is
expected. Coastal residents in the warned area should be alert
for rising water, and take appropriate action to protect life and
property.

A High Surf Warning means that high surf will affect beaches,
producing rip currents, sneaker waves and beach erosion. Stay
well back from the water's edge and be alert for exceptionally
high waves.

Keep away from large logs on the beach. Water running up on the
beach can lift or roll logs which can injure or kill someone
caught in their path.

properties.areaDesc: Clatsop County Coast; Tillamook County Coast
properties.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 13 at 12:40PM PST until November 14 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Portland OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Warning, large waves and dangerous surf
conditions. Breakers up to 30 to 35 feet. For the Coastal Flood
Advisory, tidal overflow flooding expected.

* WHERE...Clatsop and Tillamook Coast.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, until noon PST Saturday. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding, up to one foot above ground level,
during high tides is expected in the low lying areas near bays,
sloughs, and the lower reaches of the coastal rivers.
Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties, and other
structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off rocks and
jetties and drown while observing high surf. Severe beach
erosion may destroy coastal properties and buildings. Higher
than normal water run-up is expected on beaches and low-lying
shoreline.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The threat of sneaker waves is extreme
during these scenarios. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock people
off of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid ocean
which may lead to serious injury or drowning. The sneaker wave
threat will peak Friday evening into Friday night. In addition,
the Tongue Point tidal gage in Astoria is forecast to reach
approximately 10.5 feet during high tide this afternoon, which
is high enough to result in tidal overflow flooding for a few
hours around high tide.

properties.areaDesc: San Diego County Coastal Areas; Orange County Coastal
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 13 at 12:15PM PST until November 15 at 10:00AM PST by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5 to
7 feet with sets 8 to 10 feet along west-facing beaches. For the
Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding expected,
particularly along west-facing beaches where surf will be
highest.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, from 4 PM this afternoon to
10 AM PST Sunday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 7 AM to
4 PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Dangerous swimming and
surfing conditions and localized beach erosion.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Adjusted high tides will be near 6.2-6.5
feet around midday on Saturday, which will combine with high
surf to produce minor coastal flooding. Highest surf is expected
to occur late Saturday into early Sunday. Surf begins to wane
Sunday afternoon but will remain elevated into Monday.

properties.areaDesc: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 13 at 12:05PM PST until November 14 at 6:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10
to 15 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the High Surf
Warning, dangerously large breaking waves of 18 to 25 feet
with dangerous rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Warning,
moderate to significant coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches. Surf will we highest for west-
northwest facing beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST this
evening. For the High Surf Warning, from 9 PM this evening to
3 AM PST Sunday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 3 AM to 6
PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...There is a high risk for flooding of sea water over
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide. This includes significant flooding of coastal
beaches, walkways and roads, and potentially damaging some
structures. Significant beach erosion is expected. Powerful
waves and strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of
ocean drowning and damage to coastal structures like piers and
jetties. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people
off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.
Remain far away from the water's edge.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of west-northwesterly swells will
create an extended period of large surf into next week, with the
potential for WARNING level surf again late Sunday night through
Monday. Areas that may see most significant impacts will be
west-northwest facing beaches, with widespread flooding likely
at low lying areas such as at Oceano Dunes. Breaking waves may
impact the Cayucos and Pismo Beach piers as well as the Morro
Bay Harbor entrance.

infrastructure.

properties.areaDesc: Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 13 at 12:05PM PST until November 17 at 3:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5 to
8 feet today, increasing to 8 to 12 feet Saturday. Surf heights
are expected to decrease to 5 to 9 feet Sunday through Tuesday.
Dangerous rip currents expected. For the Coastal Flood
Advisory, minor to moderate coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches. Surf will
we highest for west-northwest facing beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 3 PM PST Tuesday. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 4 AM to 4 PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas that are normally dry,
especially around the time of high tide, including over beach
parking lots, bike paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate to
significant beach erosion is likely. Isolated damage is unlikely
but possible. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning.
Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large
breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of significant west- northwesterly
swells are expected to produce large surf into next week with
highest surf and greatest impacts likely peaking Saturday and
potentially again Monday. Minor to moderate coastal flooding
impacts are possible, especially when largest surf overlaps
with peak high tides. Some of these impacts may be moderate to
significant beach erosion and shallow flooding of normally dry
beaches and walkways.
properties.instruction:

near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.areaDesc: Lassen Volcanic National Park; Sierra Nevada of Sierra-Nevada-Placer Counties Above 5000 ft Including Interstate 80; Sierra Nevada of El Dorado-Amador-Northern Alpine Counties Above 5000 ft Including Highway 50; Sierra Nevada of Calaveras-Tuolumne-Southern Alpine Counties Above 5000 ft
properties.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued November 13 at 12:01PM PST until November 14 at 10:00AM PST by NWS Sacramento CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Snow is expected for elevations above 6000 feet. Total snow
accumulations 6 to 12 inches, with up to 18 inches at the highest
peaks. Minor accumulations of around an 2 inch possible down to
5000 feet. Winds could gust as high as 60 mph.

* WHERE...Northern Sierra above 6000 feet, including Highway 50,
Interstate 80, State Route 4, State Route 108, Southern Cascades
above 6000 feet, including Lassen National Park.

* WHEN...Until 10 AM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. The hazardous conditions
will impact the Friday evening commute. Strong winds could cause
downed tree branches, localized power outages, and reduced
visibilities.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snow levels 6500 to 7500 feet Today, dropping
to 5500 to 6000 feet Saturday morning. Heaviest snowfall expected
this afternoon through the overnight hours. Snowfall rates of 1 to
2 inches per hour, with locally up to 3 inches per hour in
convective bands. Light flurries to 2 inches possible down to 5000
feet with higher accumulations remaining above 6000 feet. Lull in
activity Saturday afternoon through Sunday, followed by additional
snow Sunday night through Monday.
properties.instruction:
Check the latest road conditions from Caltrans online at
quickmap.dot.ca.gov or dial 5 1 1.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued November 13 at 1:53PM CST until November 14 at 9:00AM CST by NWS Chicago IL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Extreme Southeast Central Cook County in northeastern
Illinois...
Central Lake IN County in northwestern Indiana...

* WHEN...Until 900 AM CST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding
may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Storm drains and
ditches may be clogged with debris, increasing the risk of
flooding.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 153 PM CST, Doppler radar indicated lake effect rain. Minor
flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly in the advisory
area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain has fallen since Thursday
evening. Several creeks and streams are rising, including the
Turkey Creek near Merrillville which has recently risen above
bankfull.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are expected over the
area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
The Far East side of Chicago, Hammond, Gary, Calumet City,
Merrillville, South Shore, East Chicago, Schererville, Hobart,
Lansing, Crown Point, Highland, Munster, Cedar Lake, Griffith,
Dyer, South Deering, St. John, Lake Station, Lynwood, Lakes of
the Four Seasons, Whiting, Winfield and New Chicago.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
A Flood Advisory means minor flooding along waterways and other poor
drainage areas is imminent or may already be occurring. Persons in
the advisory area should use caution and avoid flood waters.

waterways.

* WHERE...Ocean and Coastal Ocean.

* WHEN...Until 4 AM EST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...At this level, flooding begins on the most
vulnerable roads in coastal and bayside communities, and along
inland tidal waterways. Some partial or full road closures are

properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory means that minor tidal flooding is
expected. Minor tidal flooding often results in some road
closures. Usually, the most vulnerable roadways will flood.

Do not leave your vehicle at a location that is prone to tidal
flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The
water may be deeper than you think it is. You will be putting
yourself in danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to
costly repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

properties.headline: Gale Warning issued November 13 at 11:27AM PST until November 13 at 7:00PM PST by NWS Medford OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...South winds 25 to 35 kt with gusts up to 40 kt and very
steep and hazardous, chaotic seas building to 25 to 30 ft at
19 seconds this evening. Then, tonight into Saturday morning,
southwest winds 20 to 30 kt tonight with very steep and
hazardous seas 25 to 30 ft at 18 seconds. Saturday afternoon
and evening, south winds 35 to 45 kt with gusts 55 to 60 kt
and seas 19 to 25 ft at 16 seconds expected.

* WHERE...All the area.

PST Sunday.

or damage vessels. Visibilities will be significantly reduced.

Saturday and Saturday night with the potential for storm force
winds and very steep and hazardous seas. This front will be
followed by another round of very high westerly swell Sunday
into Monday. Please continue to monitor the forecast for
updates on this high impact weather pattern.
properties.instruction:
Mariners should remain in port, alter course, and/or secure the
vessel for very strong winds and very steep and hazardous seas.

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 14 at 5:08AM ChST until November 14 at 4:00PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
* WHAT...Large breaking waves of 7 to 9 feet in the surf zone.
Dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...North facing reefs of the Marianas.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM ChST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The long-period north swell that originated
from Typhoon Cempaka has most likely peaked yesterday, but could
take time to subside. Therefore, large surf and dangerous rip
currents will likely continue through this afternoon.
properties.instruction:
Rip currents will be life threatening. Inexperienced swimmers
should remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents will be life threatening. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: South Central Oregon Coast; Curry County Coast
properties.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 13 at 10:23AM PST until November 16 at 10:00PM PST by NWS Medford OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous, large breaking waves of 20 to 25 ft this
morning, increasing to a peak of 30 to 35 ft late this
afternoon through Saturday morning. Another round of dangerous
surf conditions is expected Sunday night, with breaking waves
reaching 25 to 30 ft and persisting into Monday morning. Waves
gradually diminish through Monday evening, but remain
hazardous through the day.

* WHERE...Beaches of South Central Oregon Coast and Curry County
Coast. This includes Charleston, Port Orford, Gold Beach, and
Brookings.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM PST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Extremely large breaking waves will create very
hazardous conditions along beaches and area shorelines. Waves
will inundate beaches and surge into normally dry areas.
Infrastructure damage and significant beach erosion can be
expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Breaking waves will briefly ease Saturday
night to 15 to 20 ft, but quickly rise to dangerous heights
again Sunday afternoon and evening.
properties.instruction:
Beaches and coastlines will become dangerous due to very large
and life-threatening surf conditions. Stay off of beaches, rocks,
jetties,piers, and other waterside infrastructure.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 13 at 10:51AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Sanford affecting Seminole County.

.Heavy rainfall has caused river levels on the St. Johns near Sanford
to remain just at Minor Flood Stage. The river is forecast to remain
steady around Minor Flood Stage into next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Sanford...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Sanford.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 5.5 feet, Water surrounds homes and covers some
driveways in the Stone Island area near Enterprise in Volusia
County. Water enters yards and floods docks in the River Oaks
Estates subdivision.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:30 AM EST Friday the stage was 5.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 4.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage just
after midnight tonight and continue rising to 5.5 feet just after
midnight tonight. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 5.5 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

through Monday.

properties.headline: Blizzard Warning issued November 13 at 6:07AM AKST until November 15 at 7:00AM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Blizzard conditions. Additional snow accumulations up to two
inches. Winds gusting as high as 45 mph through Friday, then 60 mph
Saturday into Sunday.

* WHERE...Central and Eastern Beaufort Sea Coast.

* WHEN...Until 7 AM AKST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult. Snow and blowing snow could
reduce visibility below one half mile at times. Periods of blizzard
conditions will be intermittently possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...We are expecting a lull in snowfall beginning
Friday afternoon through Saturday evening before snowfall chances
increase Saturday night into Sunday morning. With the lull in snow
and winds, expect higher visibilities. Winds will increase
thereafter and be strongest on Saturday afternoon into Sunday with
gusts as high as 60 mph possible, with blizzard conditions
returning.
properties.instruction:
Travel should be restricted to emergencies only. A Blizzard Warning
means severe winter weather conditions are expected or occurring.
Falling and blowing snow with strong winds are likely. This could
lead to whiteout conditions, making travel extremely dangerous. If
you must travel, have a winter survival kit with you. If you get
stranded, stay in your vehicle.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National Seashore; San Francisco Peninsula Coast; Northern Monterey Bay
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued November 13 at 3:44AM PST until November 13 at 6:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, An increased risk for
sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of
15 to 20 ft expected. For the High Surf Warning, Dangerously
large breaking waves of 25 to 35 ft, with occasional sets of
40 to 50 ft at favored breakpoints. For the Coastal Flood
Advisory, large breaking waves will run up beaches and crash
over seawalls, inundating adjacent, low-lying infrastructure.

* WHERE...Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National
Seashore, San Francisco Peninsula Coast and Northern Monterey
Bay.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through this afternoon.
For the High Surf Warning, from 6 PM today to 4 AM PST Sunday.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from midnight tonight to 6 PM
PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower
swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and
increasing the risk of drowning. Waves can sweep across the
shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from
beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The Coastal Flood Advisory on Saturday is
specifically for the Pacific Coast, where large breaking waves
will spill over sea walls and run up beaches onto adjacent
infrastructure.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other waterside
infrastructure.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

Shoreline.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM PST today.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tide gauge, high tide
is expected to be: 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 12:49 PM
today 11/13. These predictions include up to 1.8 ft of surge

Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 13 at 3:44AM PST until November 13 at 4:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the first Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 1.5 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards
Statement, An increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip
currents with breaking waves of 15 to 20 ft expected. For the
High Surf Warning, Dangerously large breaking waves of 25 to
35 ft, with occasional sets of 40 to 50 ft at favored
breakpoints. For the second Coastal Flood Advisory, large
breaking waves will run up beaches and crash over seawalls,
inundating adjacent, low-lying infrastructure.

* WHERE...San Francisco and Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur
Coast.

* WHEN...For the first Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST
today. For the Beach Hazards Statement, through this afternoon.
For the High Surf Warning, from 6 PM today to 4 AM PST Sunday.
For the second Coastal Flood Advisory, from midnight tonight to
6 PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower
swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and
increasing the risk of drowning. Waves can sweep across the
shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from
beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tide gauge, high tide
is expected to be: 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 12:49 PM
today 11/13. These predictions include up to 1.8 ft of surge
that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the
Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
The Coastal Flood Advisory on Saturday is specifically for the
Pacific Coast, where large breaking waves will spill over sea
walls and run up beaches onto adjacent infrastructure.
properties.instruction:

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other waterside
infrastructure.

infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,

properties.areaDesc: Mason, WA
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued November 13 at 2:24AM PST until November 15 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Seattle WA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of northwest Washington, including the following
county, Mason.

* WHEN...Through late Saturday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Three to four and a half inches of rain is forecast for the south
slopes of the Olympics between early Friday and early Sunday with
snow levels of 5500 to 6500 feet. The combination of heavy rain
and relatively high snow levels could push the Skokomish River
near Potlatch above flood stage.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.areaDesc: Greater Lake Tahoe Area; Greater Lake Tahoe Area
properties.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued November 13 at 1:32AM PST until November 14 at 10:00AM PST by NWS Reno NV
properties.description:
* CHANGES...None.

* WHAT...Heavy wet snow. Snow accumulations near 12 inches above 7000
feet, with up to 6 inches below 7000 feet. Snow accumulations up to
20 inches along the crest west of Lake Tahoe. Wind gusts of 70 to
90 mph over ridges and gusts of 45 to 55 mph for Truckee and Lake
Tahoe communities. Wave heights 2 to 5 feet on Lake Tahoe.

* WHERE...Greater Lake Tahoe Area.

* WHEN...From 10 AM this morning to 10 AM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. The hazardous conditions
could impact the Friday evening commute. Strong winds and Sierra
cement snow could cause damage to trees and power lines. Strong
winds and rough waves on Lake Tahoe will create hazardous
conditions for small watercraft.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A burst of heavy snow is likely with this
system late this afternoon into the evening with snow levels
falling to as low as 5500 feet.
properties.instruction:
If you must travel, keep an extra flashlight, food, and water in your
vehicle in case of an emergency. The latest road conditions for the
state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.

properties.areaDesc: Harlan; Letcher
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 12 at 8:10PM EST by NWS Jackson KY
properties.description:
Multiple rounds of showers, mostly rain in the valleys and snow at
higher elevations, are expected on Friday and Friday night.
Temperatures should be cold enough for minor snow accumulations at
elevations above 2,500 feet with mainly a dusting to half inch on
grassy and elevated surfaces. However, localized 1 to 2 inch snow
accumulations are possible over the highest portions of Big Black
Mountain. The snowfall combined with air temperatures falling deep in
the 20s could yield a few slippery spots over the highest portions of
Highway 160  near the Kentucky-Virginia state line, especially on
Friday night.
properties.instruction:
Monitor the weather situation closely and be alert for threatening
weather conditions.

properties.areaDesc: Harlan; Letcher
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 12 at 1:42PM EST by NWS Jackson KY
properties.description:
Multiple rounds of showers, mostly rain in the valleys and snow at
higher elevations, are expected on Friday and Friday night.
Temperatures should be cold enough for minor snow accumulations at
elevations of 2,500 feet, mainly a dusting to half inch on grassy and
elevated surfaces. However, localized 1 to 2 inch snow accumulations
are possible over the highest portions of Big Black Mountain. The
snowfall combined with air temperatures falling deep in the 20s could
yield a few slippery spots over the highest portions of Highway 160
near the Kentucky-Virginia state line, especially on Friday night.
properties.instruction:
Monitor the weather situation closely and be alert for threatening
weather conditions.
